objective: Converge Tisha event-only permission and the exact registered-event tag onto the accepted canonical HighLevel outbox without sending, enrolling, or mutating a provider.
implementation: Audit the migration ledger and add only the next globally free forward-only migration if contact-scoped permission, durable global email restrictions, cancellation, or identity ambiguity cannot be represented by the applied schema; never edit applied 2220.

Create one shared typed evaluator with exact precedence: complaint or hard bounce; contact suppression or email/all DND; global unsubscribe; event withdrawal or registration cancellation; invalid, archived, mismatched, or ambiguous identity; missing active event permission.

Atomically resolve or create exactly one adult contact for the scoped normalized email without granting generic or marketing consent, persist registration plus permission history/current projection, and enqueue one deterministic held HighLevel outbox event in the same transaction.
Do not call the legacy direct HighLevel client, enroll a workflow directly, or automatically queue the Resend fallback. Preserve historical rows as immutable history.

Extend the canonical producer and dispatcher for the new event, exact two-tag projection, account/product/contact/event matching, and a second eligibility check immediately before provider operations.

Do not silently reuse or flip a held row created with transport_mode=disabled. A later live canary requires one explicit exact-row prepare transition bound to the delivery key, run, allowlist, budget, current eligibility, no-prior-effect proof, and audit.

After the provider add-tags operation, require a provider readback proving both exact tags before completing the operation receipt. Ambiguous or missing readback is uncertain and cannot be replayed automatically.

Make the exact-key reprocess command read-only by default. It returns only sanitized hashes, eligibility reason, outbox state, and would-enqueue state while changing zero rows and making zero provider calls.

If an explicit enqueue path is retained, keep it separately authorization-gated and limited to deterministic outbox insertion; replay must be a duplicate/no-op and it must never call GHL or a fallback directly.
required_tests: Full typed precedence table, pairwise collisions, and fail-closed unknown/missing states.
Atomic registration, adult contact, event-only permission history/current projection, and exactly one held outbox row.
No newsletter/general-marketing consent and no backfill/inference for legacy rows.
Replay creates no duplicate; withdrawal/suppression cannot be overridden.
Post-claim DND, withdrawal, complaint, or hard bounce causes zero provider operations.
Exact-row canary preparation refuses a disabled held row without matching run, allowlist, budget, current eligibility, and no-prior-effect proof.
Provider tag readback must prove both exact tags; missing or ambiguous readback becomes uncertain with no automatic replay.
Account, product, contact, registration, and event-scope mismatch denial.
Read-only inspection preserves all rows, bytes, and timestamps.
Provider-off deployment yields zero adapter calls, messages, enrollments, or GHL mutations.
PostgreSQL 16 and 18, migration safety/checksum, focused unit/integration, typecheck, build, lint, scoped format, secret scan, and diff check.
forbidden: No GHL UI change, workflow activation, manual tag, direct enrollment, provider send, WhatsApp, fallback email, repeated signup, or live reprocess.
No production or persistent-staging provider/config mutation.
No inference of event permission from deliverability, newsletter consent, historical enrollment, or the 207 contacts.
Do not cherry-pick the historical PR 106, PR 111, or PR 112 direct-provider implementations.

handoff.required_result: One sanitized handoff with exact head, changed paths, migration checksum if any, tests, zero-effects readback, conflicts, and remaining separately gated live proof.
